elements.element: Transition assistance obligation on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason ... provide reasonable transition assistance to Corio and its Customers"

elements.element: Assistance available for up to 6 months
elements.evidence: "for a period of up to six (6) months"

elements.element: Return of Customer Data within 30 days of expiry/termination
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days of Corio's written request, return to Corio all data" — the 30-day clock runs from a later written request, not from expiry or termination

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format

elements.evidence: "thereafter delete such data and Confidential Information from its systems"
"certify such deletion to Corio in writing"
"up to six (6) months" exceeds 90 days of assistance
"within thirty (30) days of Corio's written request" — export duty is contingent on a request rather than mandatory within 30 days of exit

reasons: The inserted 11.4 covers assistance duration, then-current rates, machine-readable format, deletion and certification, so most preferred elements are present.

The data-return deadline is tied to "thirty (30) days of Corio's written request" rather than to expiry or termination; a request condition must not swallow the mandatory post-termination return, so the preferred 30-day return element fails.
The same defect also defeats the fallback element "data export within 30 days", since no export is owed unless and until Corio requests it; neither level is complete.
Fix by changing the trigger to run from exit, e.g. "within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination", leaving the rest of the insertion intact.

The insertion is otherwise minimal (a concise new clause for an absent obligation) and preserves intent, expressly stating it does not limit Corio's surviving rights under 11.3 or its retention rights.
